name: llama.cpp
description: llama.cpp runs GGUF language models directly in C/C++ with no Python runtime. This installs llama-server, which serves a built-in web chat UI plus an OpenAI-compatible API on the same port, so it can back tools like AnythingLLM, Open WebUI or Claude Code. Lighter and closer to the metal than Ollama.

app_vars.name: var_backend
app_vars.label: Build Variant
app_vars.help: auto takes vulkan for any passed-through GPU, cpu otherwise. cuda picks the CUDA 12 or 13 build from the host driver; rocm, sycl-fp16/fp32 and openvino are x64 only.

app_vars.name: var_model_repo
app_vars.label: Model Repository
app_vars.help: GGUF repo on HuggingFace, optionally with :QUANT, downloaded on first service start

app_vars.name: var_ctx_size
app_vars.label: Context Size
app_vars.help: The KV cache for this has to fit next to the model

app_vars.name: var_offload_layers
app_vars.label: GPU Layers
app_vars.help: Empty offloads every layer on a GPU build and none on cpu

app_vars.name: var_api_key
app_vars.label: API Key
app_vars.help: Clients must send it as a bearer token. Empty means no authentication

app_vars.name: INSTALL_NVIDIA_DRIVERS
app_vars.label: Install NVIDIA driver libraries
app_vars.help: Set to no when you install a matching driver in the container yourself

notes.text: On first start llama-server downloads the model set in LLAMA_ARG_HF_REPO (default: ggml-org/gemma-4-E2B-it-GGUF:Q4_0, roughly 3.5 GB with its vision projector) into /opt/llama-cpp_data/models, so the container is usable straight away. Choose another at install time with var_model_repo, or later swap it for any GGUF repo (repo or repo:QUANT), or point LLAMA_ARG_MODEL at a local file, then restart.

The web UI and the OpenAI-compatible API share port 8080: /v1/chat/completions, /v1/models and friends. There is no authentication unless an API key is set - supply one at install time or set LLAMA_ARG_API_KEY in /opt/llama-cpp.env.

The build variant is chosen at install time: cpu, vulkan (any GPU vendor), cuda (NVIDIA; CUDA 13 with a 580+ host driver, CUDA 12 otherwise), rocm (AMD, with the matching ROCm runtime from AMD's TheRock wheels), sycl-fp16/sycl-fp32 (Intel GPU, with the oneAPI runtime and Level Zero) or openvino (Intel CPU/GPU), or auto to take vulkan when a GPU is passed through. The choice is remembered in /opt/llama-cpp_data/.backend so updates keep it.
RAM is the limiting factor: the model must fit alongside the KV cache. 8 GB comfortably runs models up to roughly 7B at Q4. Raise LLAMA_ARG_CTX_SIZE only if you have headroom.

By default the build named by the latest stable llama.cpp release (vX.Y.Z) is installed. Set GH_INCLUDE_PRERELEASE=1 to follow the nightly bNNNN builds instead. The choice is remembered in /opt/llama-cpp_data/.prerelease and used by updates; GH_INCLUDE_PRERELEASE=0 or 1 on an update run switches it.
